fm_momentum_direct.description: Use signed approaches, momentum and restitution, and check impulse directions and kinetic energy after direct impacts.

sections.title: Why can impulse have a negative sign?
sections.label: Use signed velocities
sections.intro: The impulse along a chosen axis equals the change in signed momentum along that axis.

blocks.html: For one particle of constant mass, \(I=m(v-u)\).

blocks.title: Use a signed velocity change for impulse
blocks.prompt: A sphere of mass \(4\) kilograms initially moves rightwards at \(6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). A short impulse makes it move leftwards at \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Taking right as positive, find the signed impulse.

retry.feedback: The final velocity is negative because the ball moves left. Use signed velocities.

blocks.hint: A reversal of direction changes momentum by more than the change in speed suggests.
blocks.solution:
Write the initial and final velocities using the same sign convention: \(6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(-3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

The impulse is final momentum minus initial momentum, giving \(-36\,\mathrm{N\,s}\).

blocks.html: Subtracting speeds instead of signed velocities loses reversals.

sections.title: Which two equations determine the outgoing velocities?
sections.label: Conserve and compare
sections.intro: If the external impulse along the line of centres is negligible, conserve total momentum in that direction.

blocks.html: With positive axis from A to B, use \(v_B-v_A=e(u_A-u_B)\) when A approaches B along that direction.

figure.alt: Spheres A and B lie on a common line. Their two incoming velocity arrows point towards each other.
figure.caption: Choose one positive direction for both spheres. With right positive, the arrows shown give a positive velocity for A and a negative velocity for B.

blocks.title: Resolve a direct impact with signed momentum
blocks.prompt: Spheres A and B of masses \(3\) and \(5\) kilograms collide directly on a smooth horizontal track. Positive is from A towards B at contact. Their incoming signed velocities are \(7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(-1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), respectively. The coefficient of restitution is \(\frac{3}{7}\). Find both outgoing signed velocities.
blocks.hint: Use the relative approach and separation speeds along the line of impact, together with total momentum.
blocks.solution:
Momentum along the line is conserved. With outgoing velocities \(v_A\) and \(v_B\), use \(3v_A+5v_B=16\).

Apply restitution to the separation speed, \(v_B-v_A=\frac{24}{7}\). Solving gives \(- \frac{1}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for A and \(\frac{23}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for B.

blocks.html: Do not take separate momentum conservation equations for each sphere.

sections.title: What do measured outgoing velocities tell me about restitution?
sections.label: Find the missing velocity first
sections.intro: Once the incoming velocities and one outgoing velocity are known, momentum gives the other. Restitution follows from the ratio of relative speeds.

blocks.html: A record must satisfy both momentum and the restitution relation.

blocks.title: Resolve a direct impact with signed momentum
blocks.prompt: Spheres A and B of masses \(3\) and \(5\) kilograms collide directly on a smooth horizontal track. Positive is from A towards B at contact. Their incoming signed velocities are \(7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(-1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), respectively. The outgoing velocity of B is \(\frac{23}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the signed outgoing velocity of A and coefficient of restitution.
blocks.hint: Use the relative approach and separation speeds along the line of impact, together with total momentum.
blocks.solution:
Use the momentum equation with the known outgoing velocity of B. A leaves with signed velocity \(- \frac{1}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

The separation speed is \(\frac{24}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and approach speed \(8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Their ratio gives \(e=\frac{3}{7}\).

blocks.html: The ratio of one object's outgoing to incoming speed is not generally restitution for two moving spheres.

blocks.title: Resolve a direct impact with signed momentum
blocks.prompt: Spheres A and B of masses \(5\) and \(7\) kilograms collide directly on a smooth horizontal track. Positive is from A towards B at contact. Their incoming signed velocities are \(9\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(-2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), respectively. The outgoing velocity of B is \(\frac{41}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the signed outgoing velocity of A and coefficient of restitution.
blocks.hint: Use the relative approach and separation speeds along the line of impact, together with total momentum.
blocks.solution:
Use the momentum equation with the known outgoing velocity of B. A leaves with signed velocity \(-2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

The separation speed is \(\frac{55}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and approach speed \(11\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Their ratio gives \(e=\frac{5}{7}\).

sections.title: Does momentum conservation imply no energy loss?
sections.label: Compare system energies
sections.intro: With non-unit restitution, the speeds can change so that total kinetic energy falls while total momentum remains unchanged.

blocks.html: Use \(\Delta K=K_f-K_i\) for a signed change and \(K_i-K_f\) for a positive loss.

blocks.title: Resolve a direct impact with signed momentum
blocks.prompt: Spheres A and B of masses \(3\) and \(5\) kilograms collide directly on a smooth horizontal track. Positive is from A towards B at contact. Their incoming signed velocities are \(7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(-1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), respectively. The coefficient of restitution is \(\frac{3}{7}\). Find the total kinetic energy lost and the signed impulse on A.
blocks.hint: Use the relative approach and separation speeds along the line of impact, together with total momentum.
blocks.solution:
Momentum along the line is conserved. With outgoing velocities \(v_A\) and \(v_B\), use \(3v_A+5v_B=16\).

Apply restitution to the separation speed, \(v_B-v_A=\frac{24}{7}\). Solving gives \(- \frac{1}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for A and \(\frac{23}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for B.

Subtract the final system KE from the initial system KE. The energy lost is \(\frac{2400}{49}\,\mathrm J\).

The signed impulse on A is \(- \frac{150}{7}\,\mathrm{N\,s}\). The impulse on B is equal and opposite.

blocks.html: Use both spheres’ energies in the system loss.

sections.title: Can measured post-impact readings be inconsistent?
sections.label: Check relative speeds
sections.intro: Conservation of momentum alone is not enough to validate a proposed collision. It must also keep separation consistent with the assumed model.

blocks.html: Require \(0\le e\le1\). Unit restitution is perfectly elastic. At zero restitution the normal separation speed immediately after impact is zero.

blocks.title: Validate a proposed post-impact record
blocks.prompt: Two spheres of masses \(4\) and \(3\) kilograms approach along their line of centres with signed velocities \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). A proposed pair of outgoing readings is \(\frac{4}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for A and \(\frac{32}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for B. Find the inferred restitution coefficient and classify the record.
blocks.hint: Check the restitution bound even if the proposed readings conserve momentum.
blocks.solution:
The incoming relative approach speed is \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The proposed separation velocity of B relative to A is \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

Their quotient gives \(e=1\). Unit restitution gives the perfectly elastic case in this model.

blocks.html: Equal normal velocities at the instant after impact do not generally imply a permanent bond.

blocks.title: Validate a proposed post-impact record
blocks.prompt: Two spheres of masses \(6\) and \(5\) kilograms approach along their line of centres with signed velocities \(6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). A proposed pair of outgoing readings is \(- \frac{3}{22}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for A and \(\frac{81}{11}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for B. Find the inferred restitution coefficient and classify the record.
blocks.hint: Check the restitution bound even if the proposed readings conserve momentum.
blocks.solution:
The incoming relative approach speed is \(6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The proposed separation velocity of B relative to A is \(\frac{15}{2}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

Their quotient gives \(e=\frac{5}{4}\). The inferred coefficient is outside the physical interval from zero to one.

examples.title: Resolve a direct impact with signed momentum
examples.question: Spheres A and B of masses \(2\) and \(4\) kilograms collide directly on a smooth horizontal track. Positive is from A towards B at contact. Their incoming signed velocities are \(6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(- \frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), respectively. The coefficient of restitution is \(\frac{2}{7}\). Find both outgoing signed velocities.
solution: Momentum along the line is conserved. With outgoing velocities \(v_A\) and \(v_B\), use \(2v_A+4v_B=10\).

examples.title: Validate a proposed post-impact record
examples.question: Two spheres of masses \(3\) and \(2\) kilograms approach along their line of centres with signed velocities \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). A proposed pair of outgoing readings is \(\frac{9}{5}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for A and \(\frac{9}{5}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for B. Find the inferred restitution coefficient and classify the record.

examples.title: Validate a proposed post-impact record
examples.question: Two spheres of masses \(5\) and \(4\) kilograms approach along their line of centres with signed velocities \(5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). A proposed pair of outgoing readings is \(1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for A and \(5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for B. Find the inferred restitution coefficient and classify the record.

Their quotient gives \(e=\frac{4}{5}\). The coefficient is between zero and one, as for a partially elastic impact.

related.title: Smooth fixed surfaces and rebound geometry

fm_momentum_surfaces.description: Reverse and scale the normal component, preserve tangential motion and use the post-impact direction in further calculations.

sections.title: Which component can a smooth wall change?
sections.label: Split normal and tangent
sections.intro: A smooth wall exerts a perpendicular impulse, so the tangential component of the sphere’s momentum cannot change during that collision.

blocks.html: Reverse and scale the normal component. Preserve the signed tangent component.

figure.alt: An incident path approaches a vertical wall at P. Its rebounding path leaves the wall while continuing in the same tangential sense.
figure.caption: The smooth wall changes only the normal component. The two path angles are measured relative to the wall itself.

blocks.title: Apply restitution normal to a smooth wall
blocks.prompt: A sphere of mass \(\frac{3}{2}\) kilograms strikes a fixed smooth vertical wall. Before impact its signed velocity perpendicular to the wall is \(-5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), taking away from the wall as positive. Its signed component parallel to the wall is \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The coefficient of restitution is \(\frac{1}{3}\). Give both outgoing signed components.

retry.feedback: The ball moves away from the wall after impact, so the normal component is positive.

blocks.hint: Separate the normal direction from the tangent. The wall supplies impulse, so do not conserve the ball’s normal momentum.
blocks.solution:
Reverse the normal component and multiply its magnitude by the restitution coefficient.

There is no tangential impulse. The final normal component is \(\frac{5}{3}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and the parallel component remains \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

blocks.html: Do not multiply the whole velocity by restitution.

sections.title: How do I state the rebound speed and angle?
sections.label: Combine outgoing components
sections.intro: Use the two outgoing components to form a right triangle, then measure the angle from the reference requested.

blocks.html: An angle to the wall uses the tangent component adjacent to it and the normal component opposite.

blocks.title: Apply restitution normal to a smooth wall
blocks.prompt: A sphere of mass \(\frac{3}{2}\) kilograms strikes a fixed smooth vertical wall. Before impact its signed velocity perpendicular to the wall is \(-5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), taking away from the wall as positive. Its signed component parallel to the wall is \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The coefficient of restitution is \(\frac{1}{3}\). Find its exact speed and the tangent of its acute rebound angle to the wall.

fields.label: Tangent of rebound angle to wall

blocks.hint: Separate the normal direction from the tangent. The wall supplies impulse, so do not conserve the ball’s normal momentum.
blocks.solution:
The two outgoing components are \(\frac{5}{3}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) normal and \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) parallel.

Pythagoras gives exact speed \(\frac{\sqrt{106}}{3}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The angle to the wall has tangent \(\frac{5}{9}\).

blocks.html: An angle to the wall is complementary to its angle to the normal.

sections.title: How can I use a rebound angle to find restitution?
sections.label: Recover the normal speed
sections.intro: On a smooth wall the tangential speed carried through the collision links the rebound angle to the outgoing normal speed.

blocks.html: Compare this normal speed with the incoming normal speed to obtain restitution.

blocks.title: Apply restitution normal to a smooth wall
blocks.prompt: A sphere of mass \(\frac{3}{2}\) kilograms strikes a fixed smooth vertical wall. Before impact its signed velocity perpendicular to the wall is \(-5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), taking away from the wall as positive. Its signed component parallel to the wall is \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The tangent of the angle its outgoing velocity makes with the wall is \(\frac{5}{9}\). Find the coefficient of restitution and the magnitude of the impulse.
blocks.hint: Separate the normal direction from the tangent. The wall supplies impulse, so do not conserve the ball’s normal momentum.
blocks.solution:
Smooth contact leaves the velocity parallel to the wall unchanged. The outgoing normal component is the tangent of the rebound angle multiplied by that parallel speed.

This gives normal rebound speed \(\frac{5}{3}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), so \(e=\frac{1}{3}\).

The change of normal momentum gives impulse magnitude \(10\,\mathrm{N\,s}\).

blocks.html: Compare normals, not two whole speed magnitudes.

blocks.title: Apply restitution normal to a smooth wall
blocks.prompt: A sphere of mass \(\frac{5}{2}\) kilograms strikes a fixed smooth vertical wall. Before impact its signed velocity perpendicular to the wall is \(-7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), taking away from the wall as positive. Its signed component parallel to the wall is \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The tangent of the angle its outgoing velocity makes with the wall is \(\frac{7}{6}\). Find the coefficient of restitution and the magnitude of the impulse.
blocks.hint: Separate the normal direction from the tangent. The wall supplies impulse, so do not conserve the ball’s normal momentum.
blocks.solution:
Smooth contact leaves the velocity parallel to the wall unchanged. The outgoing normal component is the tangent of the rebound angle multiplied by that parallel speed.

This gives normal rebound speed \(\frac{14}{3}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), so \(e=\frac{2}{3}\).

The change of normal momentum gives impulse magnitude \(\frac{175}{6}\,\mathrm{N\,s}\).

sections.title: Why does tangential motion cancel in the energy loss?
sections.label: Compare the changed parts
sections.intro: The wall changes the sphere's normal momentum. Its unchanged tangential speed contributes the same energy before and after.

blocks.html: Compute impulse and KE change from the normal components.

blocks.title: Apply restitution normal to a smooth wall
blocks.prompt: A sphere of mass \(\frac{3}{2}\) kilograms strikes a fixed smooth vertical wall. Before impact its signed velocity perpendicular to the wall is \(-5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), taking away from the wall as positive. Its signed component parallel to the wall is \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The coefficient of restitution is \(\frac{1}{3}\). Find the energy loss and impulse magnitude.
blocks.hint: Separate the normal direction from the tangent. The wall supplies impulse, so do not conserve the ball’s normal momentum.
blocks.solution:
Only the normal velocity changes, from \(-5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to \(\frac{5}{3}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

The tangential KE cancels. The energy loss is \(\frac{50}{3}\,\mathrm J\) and impulse magnitude \(10\,\mathrm{N\,s}\).

blocks.html: Momentum of the sphere alone is not conserved in the normal direction.

sections.title: What changes if the surface is the floor?
sections.label: Restart free flight after impact
sections.intro: A smooth horizontal floor affects vertical velocity only. Once contact ends, the outgoing components initialise a new projectile stage.

blocks.html: Use gravity after the bounce and the unchanged horizontal speed in the new flight.

blocks.title: Find the maximum height after an oblique floor impact
blocks.prompt: A ball strikes a fixed smooth level floor with horizontal speed \(5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and downwards speed \(6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Restitution is \(\frac{3}{7}\). Take \(g=10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find its vertical rise and the horizontal distance to the next impact.
blocks.hint: Apply restitution during contact, then apply gravity only during the flight.
blocks.solution:
Horizontal speed is unchanged, and restitution gives upwards speed \(\frac{18}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

Use vertical constant acceleration after the impact. The height gain is \(\frac{81}{245}\,\mathrm m\) and the non-zero return time is \(\frac{18}{35}\,\mathrm s\).

The horizontal distance before the next impact is \(\frac{18}{7}\,\mathrm m\).

blocks.html: Do not treat the impulse as if it acts throughout the flight.

blocks.title: Find the maximum height after an oblique floor impact
blocks.prompt: A ball strikes a fixed smooth level floor with horizontal speed \(7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and downwards speed \(8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Restitution is \(\frac{5}{7}\). Take \(g=10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find its vertical rise and the horizontal distance to the next impact.
blocks.hint: Apply restitution during contact, then apply gravity only during the flight.
blocks.solution:
Horizontal speed is unchanged, and restitution gives upwards speed \(\frac{40}{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

Use vertical constant acceleration after the impact. The height gain is \(\frac{80}{49}\,\mathrm m\) and the non-zero return time is \(\frac{8}{7}\,\mathrm s\).

The horizontal distance before the next impact is \(8\,\mathrm m\).

examples.title: Apply restitution normal to a smooth wall
examples.question: A sphere of mass \(1\) kilograms strikes a fixed smooth vertical wall. Before impact its signed velocity perpendicular to the wall is \(-4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), taking away from the wall as positive. Its signed component parallel to the wall is \(\frac{5}{2}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The tangent of the angle its outgoing velocity makes with the wall is \(\frac{4}{15}\). Resolve along the line of centres. The mutual impulses act only along that line, so the two tangential components remain \(\frac{5}{3}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(-3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

Combine the two perpendicular components in the original axes. A leaves with component pair \(\left(- \frac{37}{10},\frac{42}{5}\right)\).
